text: Walt Disney Imagineering Research & Development, Inc.—commonly known as Walt Disney Imagineering, Imagineering, or WDI—is the research and development arm of the Walt Disney Company, responsible for the creation, design, and construction of Disney theme parks and attractions worldwide. The company also operates Disney Live Entertainment and the Muppets Studio and manages Disney's properties, including Walt Disney Studios in Burbank and New Amsterdam Theatre and Times Square Studios Ltd. in New York City. Founded on December 16, 1952, by Walt Disney to oversee Disneyland Park's production, it was initially named Walt Disney, Inc., then renamed WED Enterprises in 1953 using the initials of Walter Elias Disney. In 1961, WED moved into the Grand Central Business Park, and in 1965, Walt Disney Productions acquired WED Enterprises, including its name. The unit was renamed Walt Disney Imagineering in January 1986, and in 1996, Disney Development Company merged into Imagineering. Imagineering created Disney Fair, which premiered in September 1996 and was discontinued after poor attendance; it was later renamed DisneyFest and opened in Singapore on October 30, 1997. By 1997, Imagineers were spread across several buildings in Grand Central Business Park, and in September 1999, Disney Imagineering announced a redesign of the park into the Grand Central Creative Campus, which included new office-studio facilities for sound stages, production, and offices. As part of a 2018 strategic reorganization, Walt Disney Parks and Resorts merged with Disney Consumer Products and Interactive Media into Disney Parks, Experiences and Products (DPEP), giving Imagineering oversight of merchandise, games, and publishing. In July 2021, DPEP chairman Josh D'Amaro announced that approximately 2,000 DPEP positions would be relocated over the next few years to Lake Nona, Orlando, Florida, with up to 90% of those being Imagineering positions, as the headquarters would move from Glendale to a 60-acre campus in Lake Nona, motivated by $570 million in Florida tax breaks, a business-friendly climate, lower cost of living, and no state income tax. However, the relocation was canceled in May 2023 due to a feud with Florida Governor Ron DeSantis. The company developed new concepts such as the Soarin' Over California ride, inspired by an erector set found by Imagineer Mark Sumner, which simulates hang gliding. Imagineering uses "blue sky speculation" to generate ideas without constraints, and it can take up to five years for an idea to become a finished attraction, with the belief that "if it can be dreamt, it can be built." WDI partnered with the Khan Academy to create "Imagineering in a Box," a series of online video classes on theme park design, divided into three categories: Creating Worlds, Designing Attractions, and Bringing Characters to Life. Past Imagineers have shared 15 principles of Imagineering, organized into five tiers: Tier 1 includes Story, Creative Intent, Attention to Detail, Theming, and Long, Medium, and Close Shots; Tier 2 includes Wienies, Transitions, Storyboards, and Pre-Shows and Post-Shows; Tier 3 includes Forced Perspective, "Read"-ability, and Kinetics; Tier 4 includes The "It's a Small World" Effect and Hidden Mickeys; and Tier 5 is Walt’s Cardinal Rule, "Plussing," which emphasizes continuous improvement and innovation, such as the rework of the Museum of the Weird into The Haunted Mansion. Disney theme parks are storytelling and visual experiences, using theming, atmosphere, and attention to detail, with techniques like forced perspective—seen in Cinderella Castle, which appears taller due to smaller upper elements—being compared to film-making. The Pirates of the Caribbean attraction evokes a buccaneer adventure, while Disney Cruise Line ships offer an elegant seafaring feel; minor details like menu names, dish titles, and Cast Member costumes are crucial. Main Street, U.S.A. features a bakery fragrance reminiscent of 1900s suburban America. Imagineering has also designed retail stores, galleries, and hotels with specific moods, such as the Disney's Contemporary Resort, which features an A-frame structure, modern décor, and a quiet monorail. In 2010, Disney Educational Products released "The Science of Disney Imagineering," a series of videos by Imagineer Asa Kalama covering science topics like Gravity, Trajectory, Levers & Pulleys, Fluids, Energy, Design & Models, Magnetism, Motion, Animal Adaptations: Communication, Friction, and Electricity, each linked to a Disney attraction. In 1991, Marty Sklar presented ten commandments attributed to Mickey Steinberg. Imagineering holds over 300 patents in areas such as advanced audio systems, fiber optics, interactive technology, live entertainment, ride systems, and special effects, and pioneered technologies like Circle-Vision 360° and FastPass. It is known for developing Audio-Animatronics, a form of 3D robotics, originating from Walt Disney’s fascination with a mechanical bird in New Orleans, first used in The Enchanted Tiki Room, and later in the 1964 World's Fair with the first human Audio-Animatronic, Abraham Lincoln, in "Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln." Audio-Animatronics are now featured in attractions like Pirates of the Caribbean, The Haunted Mansion, The Hall of Presidents, Country Bear Musical Jamboree, Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance, and Tiana's Bayou Adventure, with some, like Mr. Potato Head at Toy Story Mania!, capable of interacting with guests. WEDway, a people mover using linear induction motor technology, operates at Magic Kingdom and George Bush Intercontinental Airport, with a version with rubber wheels every 9 feet used at Disneyland from 1967 to 1995. Since 1952, Imagineering has created twelve theme parks, a town, seven cruise ships, dozens of resort hotels, water parks, shopping centers, sports complexes, and entertainment venues. Former creative director John Hench designed the "Tower of Nations" for the 1960 Winter Olympics opening and closing ceremonies, with Walt Disney serving as Pageantry Committee chairman. Imagineering has collaborated with Disney Consumer Products on store designs, including the first Glendale Disney Store, the now-defunct Walt Disney Gallery in Santa Ana, a Roman-themed store at The Forum Shops in Las Vegas, and the World of Disney flagship stores in resorts, Lake Buena Vista, Anaheim, New York City, and Disneyland Paris. In 2009, an overhaul of Disney Stores was planned with input from Apple CEO Steve Jobs to transition to an interactive entertainment hub. In the 1990s, Imagineering designed the 24,000 square foot Club Disney center in Thousand Oaks and later launched DisneyQuest in 1998 at Disney Springs and in Chicago in 1999, with a 2007 design and construction of the Disney Dream and Disney Fantasy ships, as well as exhibitions for the Autry Museum of Western Heritage, the Encounter Restaurant at LAX, and exhibits for the Port Discovery museum in Baltimore and the "Below Deck" sound show in St. Augustine. From 1995 to 1997, Imagineering oversaw the renovation of the New Amsterdam Theatre and remodeled Times Square Studios in 1996 after acquiring ABC. In 1997, Disney purchased the California Angels and renamed them the Anaheim Angels, and Imagineering later renovated Anaheim Stadium. The company also worked with For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology to create the teaser video and theming for the 2016 FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Stronghold. Since the 1960s, Imagineering's headquarters have been in nondescript office buildings at the former Grand Central Airport in Glendale, California, about two miles east of Disney's Burbank corporate headquarters. Field offices exist at Epcot and Disney's Hollywood Studios at Walt Disney World Resort, and offices are also located at various other sites.
